chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one whose good deeds delight him and his evil deeds disgust him, he is a believer.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a true believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi is foundational for defining *al-iman al-akbar* (major faith) as an internal state of *muhasaba* (self-accounting), where the heart naturally reacts to deeds. It highlights that true faith is not merely ritualistic but is evidenced by the emotional congruence of the soul with divine commands, a concept central to the works of scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Qasim Bin Gurwa, from Abu Al Abbas who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘The one whose good deeds delight him, and his evil deeds disgust him, so he is a Momin’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from abu al-‘Abbas who has said that abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said the following:
“Whoever enjoys a virtuous deed and is disgusted with a sin is a believer.”
